correspondence.excerpt: A glossary entry, ontology node, source quotation, generated index row, or narrative explanation is not a Definition by itself.
Definition identity, artifact type, semantic kind, authority kind, lifecycle posture, owner scope, and bounded-context membership are independent axes.
One canonical field must never be silently inferred from another;
dependent classifications require explicit typed relations;
convenience labels are generated projections.

DefinitionComplete(d) iff StableId(d) and ExactScope(d) and FormalVoice(d) and NonNormativePlainVoice(d) and NonNormativeDomainVoice(d) and Boundaries(d) and AdmittedSources(d) and RegistryPostimage(d) and GeneratedIndex(d) and CurrentDriftRoute(d).
DefinitionComplete(d) does not imply Admitted(d).
A Definition is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic artifact that assigns a term one normative meaning within an exact authority scope.

It is structurally complete only when stable identity, applicability, exclusions, a scientific/formal normative voice, explicitly non-normative plain-language and domain-context voices, boundaries, admitted source posture, primary consumers, a synchronized registry postimage, generated index, and a current drift route are declared.
Only an exact owner promotion decision can make one exact Definition version canonical authority.

counterexamples.expected_interpretation: The combined selected source constraints cannot accept this assignment; the biconditional forces completeness while the prose then requires applicability.
counterexamples.rationale: Concrete source-precedence finding, not a reason to silently weaken the prose.
counterexamples.scenario: All ten formal-expression attributes are present, but applicability is missing.

counterexamples.expected_interpretation: Violates the meaning-change version condition. A representation-only edit with unchanged meaning is a separate case.
counterexamples.rationale: Separates semantic identity and versioning from byte representation.
counterexamples.scenario: Two declared Definition revisions of one identity have different normative meanings under the same version key.

counterexamples.expected_interpretation: Fails the exact promotion condition; fields, schema validity and evidence cannot substitute for matching promotion.
counterexamples.rationale: Hypothetical negative control only; no actual owner decision created.
counterexamples.scenario: CanonicalAuthority is asserted with only a decision targeting another owner, scope, identity or version.

instances.expected_interpretation: Can be structurally complete and remain unadmitted/noncanonical in the abstract theory. The real source/schema/render checks remain separate from any semantic-owner acceptance.
instances.rationale: Exposes completeness-versus-authority without simulating a real approval.
instances.scenario: An authored term definition declares its exact owner/scope/version, all voices, required boundaries/consumer/registry/index/drift fields and evidence, while no owner promotion decision exists.

known_losses: No whole-definition fidelity or biconditional recognizer for Definition membership; record/status predicates are primitive conditions, not generic validator correctness.
Ten-field/prose completeness mismatch retained, not resolved.
Voice preservation, meaning equality, exact owner authorization and canonical relation validity need independent semantic contracts.
Auxiliary population policies remain unresolved; complete/valid/evidenced objects are not declared universally unadmitted.

conflicts.description: Formal biconditional names ten attributes; prose necessary conditions also require applicability, exclusions and primary consumers. Both are encoded, so the combined theory forces the extra attributes whenever the ten formal attributes hold. This consequence requires source-owner resolution; no field is silently dropped.
conflicts.owner_route: role:definition-owner must decide whether to expand the formal expression, clarify shorthand, or revise the prose in a new authoritative version.

conflicts.description: One normative meaning is interpreted per exact version, term and scope. Historical versions may differ in meaning; a global timeless term-to-meaning function would prohibit legitimate semantic successors.
conflicts.owner_route: role:definition-owner must confirm per-version uniqueness and the scope of active/current lookup uniqueness.

conflicts.description: Object admission, admitted source posture, schema validity, evidence, exact promotion and canonical authority remain distinct. Non-entailment clauses are separate witness requirements; causal promotion behavior and live source posture are not inferred from the static model.
conflicts.owner_route: role:definition-owner must bind admission/promotion meanings and exact real review decisions separately from source provenance.

conflicts.description: Typed axes and generic-record model pairs expose lack of automatic inference. Actual allowed canonical values, governed typed dependencies and universal independence claims remain outside the primitive projection.
conflicts.owner_route: role:definition-owner and Classification/Typed Relation owners must review exact value/coupling contracts and inferential scope.
